attributes.title: Level 6

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use comments to create multiple sections in the editor to better organize your code?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What code might be placed underneath each comment?

❓ How do you create blank lines in the JavaScript editor?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Explain to the ninja that typing // tells the project to skip over the text that follows and move onto the next line of code. Just as when naming sprites, it’s useful to be short and descriptive when writing comments. 

💡 Encourage the ninja to use best practices when adding comments to their code. It’s helpful to space out comments in the editor, so that code can be placed in the lines between them. They can use the Enter key to create blank lines between comments. They should also add a space after the slashes in the comment, before adding the text.
steps.instructions:
Begin the project by adding code comments to organize where the code will go in the editor!


Add comments with these descriptions to the project: game set up, variable set up, 1-digit number, 2-digit number, 3-digit number.


Start each comment with // and add several blank lines between each comment.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you type let to declare 5 new variables then use an assignment operator = to assign each variable a value of 0?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What might each of the variables be used for? Why are they all assigned a value of 0?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that they can use copy (Ctrl + C) and paste (Ctrl + V) to declare multiple random number variables. They should be sure to change each variable’s name, if using the keyboard shortcut.
steps.instructions:
Declare the variables that will store the randomly selected numbers and the user’s guess.


Under // variable set up, type let and the name for the first random number variable, randNum1, then use an assignment operator = to assign the value 0 to the variable.


Create 3 more random number variables that are all assigned the value 0. Give each variable a different name by replacing 1 with the number of the variable, like randNum2, to make them easy to access and change the value of in the project.


Lastly, create a userGuess variable that is also assigned the value 0.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you set the random number variables to select a random integer from 0-9, then assign the userGuess variable to a user inputted value?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Which operator should be used to update the value of a variable? 

❓ What might the random number and user guess variables be used for?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that in JavaScript, a single equal sign = represents an assignment operator. This symbol assigns the variable named on the left to a value typed on the right of the operator.

💡 Encourage the ninja to consider what other interesting ways user input might be incorporated. In this project, there will be several different rounds where the user will guess a random number (of a variety of digit lengths), which will then be compared to the number stored by the variable.
steps.instructions:
Round 1: have the user guess a 1-digit number!


Update the values of 2 random number variables by assigning them a random integer between 0-9. Under // 1-digit number, type the names of both random number variables followed by an assignment operator = and the randint function, so that the code looks like: randNum1 = randint(0, 9)


Then, ask the user for a 1-digit number, and assign that value to the userGuess variable. Type the variable name followed by an assignment operator =


Open Game and drag out [ask for number (msg)] after the =. Replace null with a string that tells the user to select a number between 0-9, then type a comma , after the quotation marks and set the answerLength parameter to 1.


Click ▶ to see the project prompt the user to guess a 1-digit number between 0-9.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use a Boolean OR operator to show a dialog box if the user’s guess is equal to 1 of the 2 random numbers?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Why are there 2 random number variables, if the user only guesses 1 number?

❓ How is using a Boolean OR operator in JavaScript similar and different to the blocks editor?

❓ Why is using a Boolean OR operator helpful when more than one condition can be true, in order for code to run? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Point out to the ninja that they will need to press Shift + \ on their keyboards to type the | symbol.

💡 Help the ninja make the connection between the Boolean OR operator in JavaScript and the <or> Boolean in the blocks editor. Both sets of code allow a different value to be placed on either side. When placed in a conditional, the Boolean OR operator allows the code to run if 1 of the 2 conditions are true.

💡 Encourage the ninja to think about the variable comparisons in the context of this project. Because the user only has 1 guess, it’s helpful to create 2 possible options, to give them a higher chance of guessing the secret number correctly.
steps.instructions:
Check if the user guessed 1 of the 2 random numbers correctly!


Open Logic and drag [if] under the existing code under // 1-digit number. Highlight and delete true inside the parentheses of the if condition. 


The if conditional will check if the value of userGuess is equal to the value of randNum1 OR randNum2. Inside the parentheses of the if condition, check if the value of userGuess equals one of the random number values by using an equality operator (==). Then, type 2 vertical bars || to add a Boolean OR operator inside the parentheses. On the other side of the symbol, check if the value of userGuess equals the other random number value by using another equality operator (==). The code might look like:

(userGuess == randNum1 || userGuess == randNum2)

Open Game and drag [show long text (str) (layout)] inside the curly brackets { } of the if statement. Replace null with the userGuess variable, then type + to concatenate the value of the variable with a string that tells the user that they guessed correctly and are moving to the next round. Update the DialogLayout property, too.  


Click ▶ to see the dialog box appear if 1 of the 2 random numbers is guessed correctly!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you add an else condition, then concatenate strings and variables to reveal the correct values of the 2 random numbers?
steps.senseiHelp:
﻿Ask the ninja:

❓ What needs to be false in order for the code in the else condition to run?

❓ What symbol should be placed between the strings and variables in the showLongText code?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Walk through the logic of the conditional with the ninja. If the user’s guess is not equal to 1 of the 2 random numbers, then a dialog box will appear, telling the user what the correct answers were.

💡 Remind the ninja that strings are contained by quotation marks, and a plus sign + is used to join the string with a variable. Encourage the ninja to double check their work to make sure they’ve included the correct symbols and spacing.

💡 Point out to the ninja that they can test out the project by adding a sprite, then coding the sprite to say the variable’s value (before the user guesses). This will allow them to more easily test the project when the value is both correct and incorrect.

💡 Remind the ninja that they can use the setGameOverEffect function before the gameOver function to set an effect to play when the game over screen appears.
steps.instructions:
Tell the player the secret numbers if they guessed incorrectly.


Add an else condition by typing else { } after the closing curly bracket of the if condition. Place the cursor inside the curly brackets then press Enter to create a blank line inside the else condition.


Use another showLongText to create a dialog box with a string that reveals the secret numbers, then use concatenation (+) to show the values of the 2 random number variables, placing an “ or “ string in between the numbers. Update the DialogLayout property, too.


Last, add a gameOver(false) inside the else condition to end the game.


Click ▶ to test the different game outcomes.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you assign new values to the 3 random number variables and the user guess variable?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Which operator should be used to update the value of a variable? 

❓ What might a third random number variable be used for?

❓ Did you update the answerLength parameter in the askForNumber code so that the user enters a 2-digit number?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that in JavaScript, a single equal sign = represents an assignment operator. This symbol assigns the variable named on the left to a value typed on the right of the operator.

💡 Point out to the ninja that in the second round, the user will guess a 2-digit number, so the range of possible answers is greater. Adding a third random number variable gives the user a greater chance of guessing the number correctly.

💡Encourage the Ninja to use // to comment out the gameOver code in the 1-digit number section to ease testing.
steps.instructions:
Round 2: have the user guess a 2-digit number!


Update the values of 3 random number variables by assigning them a random integer between 10-99. Under // 2-digit number, type the names of the first 3 random variables followed by an assignment operator = and the randint function so that the code looks like:


randNum1 = randint(10, 99)

Then, ask the user for a 2-digit number, and assign that value to the userGuess variable. Type the variable name followed by an assignment operator =


Open Game and drag out [ask for number (msg)] after the =. Replace null with a string that tells the user to select a number between 10-99, then type a comma , and set the answerLength parameter to 2.


Click ▶ to see the project prompt the user to guess a 2-digit number between 10-99.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use Boolean OR operators to show a dialog box if the user’s guess is equal to 1 of the 3 random numbers?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What operator is used to check the value of a variable?

❓ Why are there only 2 Boolean OR operators, but 3 possible random numbers?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 If a ninja is struggling to type out the code, remind them that they can use copy (Ctrl + C) and paste (Ctrl + V) to easily copy the code, then update each variable’s name. 

💡 Remind the ninja that in JavaScript, a double equal sign == represents an equality operator. This symbol checks to see if the value typed on the left of the operator is equal to the value on the right. 

💡 Boolean OR  operators || should be placed between the code that checks if the user’s guess is equal to each of the 3 random number variables. This allows the program to run if 1 of these 3 conditions is true.
steps.instructions:
Check if the user guessed 1 of the 3 random numbers correctly!


Open Logic and drag [if] under the code under // 2-digit number. Highlight and delete true inside the parentheses of the if condition. 


The if conditional will use 2 Boolean OR operators to check if the value of userGuess equals the value of randNum1 OR randNum2 OR randNum3. Inside the parentheses of the if condition, check if the value of userGuess equals one of the random number values by using an equality operator (==). Then type 2 vertical bars || to add a Boolean OR operator inside the parentheses.


On the other side of the symbol, check if the value of userGuess equals one of the other random number values by using another equality operator (==). Type 2 more vertical bars || then use another equality operator (==) to check if the value of userGuess equals the third random number value. The code might look like:


(userGuess == randNum1 || userGuess == randNum2 || userGuess == randNum3)

Open Game and drag [show long text (str) (layout)] inside the curly brackets { } of the if statement. Replace null with the userGuess variable, then type + to concatenate the value of the variable with a string that tells the user that they guessed correctly and are moving to the next round. Update the DialogLayout property, too.  


Click ▶ to see the dialog box appear if 1 of the 3 random numbers is guessed correctly!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you add an else condition then concatenate strings and variables to show the values of the 3 random numbers?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What needs to be false in order for the code in the else condition to run?

❓ What message might you share in the showLongText code to tell the user that their guess was incorrect?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Walk through the logic of the conditional with the ninja. If the user’s guess is not equal to 1 of the 3 random numbers, then a dialog box will appear, telling the user what the correct answers were.

💡 Remind the ninja that strings are contained by quotation marks, and a plus sign + is  used to join the string with a variable. Encourage the ninja to double check their work to make sure they’ve included the correct symbols and spacing.

💡 If the ninja is struggling to test out the project in the second round, point out that they can add a sprite to the project, then have the sprite say the variable’s value (before the user guesses). This will allow the ninja to test out both rounds and dialog boxes more easily. 

💡 Remind the ninja that they can use the  setGameOverEffect function before the gameOver function to set an effect to play when the game over screen appears.
steps.instructions:
Tell the player the secret numbers if they guessed incorrectly.


Add an else condition by typing else { } after the closing curly bracket of the if condition. Create a blank line inside the curly brackets of the else condition then use another showLongText to create a dialog box with a string that reveals the secret numbers.


Use concatenation (+) to show the values of the 3 random number variables, placing an “ or “ string in between the numbers. Update the DialogLayout property, too.


Last, add a gameOver(false) inside the else condition to end the game.


Click ▶ to test the different game outcomes.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you update the maximum parameter in the randint function and the answerLength parameter in the askForNumber code?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Did you assign new values to the 4 random number variables and the user guess variable?

❓ What keyboard shortcut might you use to assign each variable a new value?

❓ What should the range of each randint value be changed to?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that they can copy (Ctrl + C) and paste (Ctrl + V) the code that assigns each variable a value, then update the variable names and parameters for the third round.

💡 Point out to the ninja that in the third round, the user will guess a 3-digit number, so the range of possible answers is greater. Adding a fourth random number variable gives the user a greater chance of guessing the number correctly.

💡Encourage the Ninja to use // to comment out the gameOver code in the 1 and 2-digit number sections to ease testing.
steps.instructions:
Round 3: have the user guess a 3-digit number!


Update the values of all 4 random number variables by assigning them a random integer between 100-999. Under // 3-digit number, type the names of the 4 variables followed by an assignment operator = and the randint function so that the code looks like:

randNum1 = randint(100, 999)

Then, ask the user for a 3-digit number, and assign that value to the userGuess variable. Type the variable name followed by an assignment operator =


Open Game and drag out [ask for number (msg)] after the =. Replace null with a string that tells the user to select a number between 100-999, then type a comma , and set the answerLength parameter to 3.


Click ▶ to see the project prompt the user to guess a 3-digit number between 100-999.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use Boolean OR operators to show a dialog box if the user’s guess is equal to 1 of the 4 random numbers?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What needs to be true in order for the code in the if condition to run?

❓ Why does the code need to individually check if the user’s guess is equal to each of the 4 random numbers?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 If a ninja is struggling to type out the code, remind them that they can copy (Ctrl + C) and paste (Ctrl + V) the code, then update each variable’s name. 

💡 When using Boolean OR operators ||, the left hand and right hand side statements are evaluated independently. To check if a single variable is equal to one of two values with a Boolean OR operator, use the variable on both sides of the operator like this:


userGuess == randNum1 || userGuess  == randNum2

The variable must be included on either side of the operator, otherwise the OR statement will still evaluate, but will likely cause bugs because of the faulty logic.
steps.instructions:
Check if the user guessed 1 of the 4 random numbers correctly!


Open Logic and drag [if] under the code under // 3-digit number. Delete true inside the parentheses of the if condition. 


The if conditional will use 3 Boolean OR operators to check if the value of userGuess equals the value of randNum1 OR randNum2 OR randNum3 OR randNum4. Inside the parentheses of the if condition, check if the value of userGuess equals one of the random number values by using an equality operator (==). Then type 2 vertical bars || to add a Boolean OR operator inside the parentheses. Repeat this to check the value of all 4 random number variables. The code might look like:

(userGuess == randNum1 || userGuess == randNum2 || userGuess == randNum3 || userGuess == randNum4)

Open Game and drag [show long text (str) (layout)] inside the curly brackets { } of the if statement. Replace null with the userGuess variable, then type + to concatenate the value of the variable with a string that tells the user that they guessed correctly and have won the game. Update the DialogLayout parameter, too.


Last, add a gameOver(true) inside the if condition to end the game in a win.


Click ▶ to see the dialog box appear if 1 of the 4 random numbers is guessed correctly!

💡 Remind the ninja that they can use the  setGameOverEffect function before the gameOver function to set an effect to play when the game over screen appears.

Add an else condition by typing else { } after the closing curly bracket of the if condition. Add a blank line inside the curly brackets of the else condition then use another showLongText to create a dialog box with a string that reveals the secret numbers.


Use concatenation (+) to show the values of the 4 random number variables, placing an “ or “ string in between the numbers. Update the DialogLayout property, too.


Last, add a gameOver(false) inside the else condition to end the game.


Click ▶ to test the different game outcomes.

steps.hints: ❓ What directions would help players understand how the game is played?
steps.senseiHelp:
﻿Ask the ninja:

❓ What background color might you use as a backdrop for the project?

❓ What directions might tell the user how to play the game? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡Remind the ninja that they can always click on the palette for one of the images in the code to open the editor. Once opened, they can hover their cursor over each individual color to find the corresponding value to use as a background color.

💡Remind the ninja that strings need to be placed inside of quotation marks and that parameters need to be separated by a comma, otherwise the code will not be able to run correctly.
steps.instructions:
Finish the project by adding a background color and directions!


Open Scene, drag out [set background color to (color)] into the editor underneath // game set up. Click between the parentheses to set a color parameter using a number 1-15.


Open Game and drag [show long text (str) (layout)] onto a blank line underneath the code to set the background color. Update the string and layout parameters, so that the dialog box shares directions for the user to follow.


Click ▶ to play the completed Guess the Number project!

subgroups.title: Guess the Number!
subgroups.introduction: Create a project in JavaScript that uses Boolean operators to prompt players to guess one of the secret numbers in a game that increases in challenge with each win.

validationItems.text: Create 4 variables and set their values to a random number each round.
Create a variable to store the user’s guesses and update its value with each response.
Display messages if the user’s guess is correct or incorrect.
Use the Boolean OR operator inside if conditional statements.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 6 of Blue Belt! Before you create your final Blue Belt project, there are a few neat tricks to learn that could take your game to the next level! In this level, you’ll learn more about Boolean and relational operators, which can be used to check if 1 or more conditions are true in a project. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 6:

badges.title: Making Big Decisions
badges.description: Use Boolean and relational operators as part of conditional statements in JavaScript.

badges.title: Package Deal
badges.description: Use a Boolean AND operator in JavaScript.

badges.title: Hard Pressed
badges.description: Check if a button is pressed as part of a conditional statement.

badges.title: Comparatively Speaking
badges.description: Use a relational operator in JavaScript.

badges.title: Reassess the Situation
badges.description: Use an assignment operator to give an existing variable a new value.

badges.title: This or That
badges.description: Use a Boolean OR operator in JavaScript.
